paper.title_en: Magnetic-Field Response of a Hyperbolic Kitaev Spin Liquid
paper.abstract_en: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on the Kekulé-colored hyperbolic {8,3} lattice by developing an infinite projected entangled-pair-state approach with flux-resolved loop-gas initialization and geometry-adapted tensor-network contraction. Under uniform and staggered [111] magnetic fields, we find markedly different many-body responses. The uniform field induces a sharp change between competing variational branches at weak field, whereas the polarization and mean plaquette flux evolve over a much broader field range under the staggered field. Exchange-energy competition helps explain the different response scales, while third-order effective Majorana models in a fixed-flux background exhibit contrasting low-energy spectra. Our results connect the geometry-dependent fractionalized structure of a solvable hyperbolic spin liquid to its many-body response under physical perturbations that break flux conservation.
